# shape-ops - context for bug hunters

Scope: `jix/src/ops/shape_ops/*.rs` (non-test parts). Bare file names (`slice.rs:123`) are in
`jix/src/ops/shape_ops/`; other paths are relative to `jix/src/` unless they start with `jix-py/`.

Facts that change how to read this code:
- Release builds have overflow checks OFF: unchecked `+`/`*` wrap in shipped wheels, panic in debug/tests.
- x86 and armv7 (32-bit) wheels ship but are never tested; every `(r.end - r.start) as usize` truncates there.
- No shape op overrides `read_as_elementwise_pipeline`: the default (storage/core_trait.rs:123-135) does a
  pull `read_data(.., None)` and wraps it in `OperandTyped::new_input`. So a shape op's pull buffer feeds the
  elementwise pipeline directly, including 0-stride dims.
- Python wrappers (index parsing, `-1` in reshape, dtype promotion for concatenate/stack) live in
  `jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs`; the core ops below never promote.

## Purpose
Lazy views that change shape/order without changing values. Three read strategies:
(1) pure re-stride forwarders - PermuteDims, InsertDim, RemoveDim (via `read_data_and_map_strides`), Broadcast
(pull: 0 strides) and Slice (step 1: forward; Plain inner: multiply strides); (2) split-and-forward - Slice
(stepped), Roll (wrap), Tile (cases A/B), Reshape, Concatenate, Stack: one or more inner push reads, each into a
sub-buffer of `out` at the right offset; (3) read-then-copy - Flip, Repeat, Tile case C, Broadcast push: pull the
inner region, then `NdCopier` into the destination. Each op also derives an `ArraySpecDynamic` (block shape,
fixed dims, scale weights, layout order) for the read-tiling heuristics.

## Contracts

### Relied on
- `read_data` contract (storage/core_trait.rs:71-107): one in-bounds range per dim, empty allowed; pull may
  return any strides (incl. 0); push writes the region at `out`'s strides and returns a view of `out`.
- Bounds: PermuteDims (permute_dims.rs:123) and RemoveDim (remove_dim.rs:136) only check ndim
  (`check_get_range_ndim`) and rely on the inner storage's `check_get_range`. Every other op checks itself.
- `out` validation is minimal: `check_out_buf` (storage/buf.rs:282-297) checks stride count == ndim and
  writability only. Extent (slice long enough for the region at its strides) and non-aliasing (no 0 stride on a
  dim longer than 1) are NOT checked anywhere; they come from the unsafe constructors' docs (buf.rs:59-123) and,
  in Python, from `numpy(out=)` validation (jix-py/src/array.rs:459-463). Shape ops trust both.
- `out` must not overlap memory any input reads (NdCopier `noalias`, util/nd_copy.rs:47-53; documented UB in
  jix-py/src/array.rs:471-485).
- Pull buffers cover their region: Plain returns exactly `strided_span_bytes` (storage/plain.rs:461-474), Scalar
  returns one item with all-0 strides (storage/scalar.rs:110-112), pool buffers expose their whole capacity
  (util/buf_pool.rs:109-119). Flip/Repeat/Tile index these with `get_unchecked`.
- `materialize_out_buf` (buf.rs:300-319): pull mode allocates UNINITIALIZED pool memory (util/buf_pool.rs:40-51)
  with strides from `strides_for_layout_order(read_layout_order)`; push mode returns `out.view_mut()`.
- `NdCopier::copy` (util/nd_copy.rs:42-55): both byte ranges must contain every touched byte, no overlap.
- `PLAIN_READ` flag (storage/params.rs:895-898): "read is a simple strided copy". Set by Plain
  (storage/plain.rs:145) and Scalar (storage/scalar.rs:70). Slice's fast path (slice.rs:145-160) reads it as "pull
  returns a borrowed view whose slice covers the requested bounding box at the returned strides".

### Provided
- Every non-empty read writes EVERY element of the region (push) or returns a buffer valid for every element
  (pull). `Array::to_ndarray_sub` `assume_init()`s its destination (array.rs:800) and pool memory is
  uninitialized, so a skipped element is an uninitialized read (UB for bool dtypes).
- `dtype()`/`ElementType` equal the inner's. Stack/Concatenate: `ArraysT::ElementType`
  (util/arr_sequence.rs:87-93, tuple impl requires one shared ET at 659-664) plus a runtime dtype-equality check
  (concatenate.rs:104-109, stack.rs:79-84). Typed elementwise ops reinterpret bytes based on this.
- `spec()`: `block_shape.len() == ndim` with entries in `1..=max(shape,1)` (asserted by
  util/test_util.rs:960-965); `read_layout_order` a permutation of `0..ndim` (it is NOT a pure hint for
  correctness: `strides_for_layout_order`, util/mod.rs:159-174, builds pull-mode strides from it - a duplicate
  gives aliasing strides, an out-of-range entry panics). Flags: InsertDim/RemoveDim keep PLAIN_READ and clear
  IS_COMPACT (insert_dim.rs:211, remove_dim.rs:196); every other op clears all flags. `as_compact()` is None.
- Shapes validated at construction: `check_shape_overflow` (error.rs:186, u64 product incl. itemsize) in Broadcast
  (broadcast.rs:65), Repeat (repeat.rs:63), Tile (tile.rs:79), Concatenate (concatenate.rs:114), Stack
  (stack.rs:95); ndim via `check_ndim` in InsertDim (insert_dim.rs:61), Stack (stack.rs:92), `IntoDimension` in
  Reshape (reshape.rs:54); Repeat/Tile require `ndim < NDIM_MAX` (repeat.rs:41-46, tile.rs:57-62) because their
  copy uses one extra internal dim. `Array::*` wrappers in mod.rs `unwrap()` (documented panics).

### Preconditions of pub(crate) unsafe fns used here
- `read_data_and_map_strides` (buf.rs:321-368), "caller should ensure the created strides are valid": the two
  closures must describe the same fixed dim correspondence in opposite directions, `inner_index` must be the same
  region re-indexed, and any dim dropped by outer2inner / given stride 0 by inner2outer must have extent exactly 1.
  Callers: PermuteDims (permute_dims.rs:126-135), InsertDim (insert_dim.rs:176-195; empty reads short-circuit at
  165-175 because an empty inserted dim cannot be expressed in the inner index), RemoveDim (remove_dim.rs:161-180).
  Established locally by `new()` validation.
- `StridedBuf::from_slice_mut` / `with_strides` / `copy_from` (buf.rs:118, 208, 221): caller guarantees in-bounds,
  non-aliasing strides for the region it will be used with. See inventory.

## Unsafe inventory
- buf.rs:364 - `transmute` of the inner pull buffer's lifetime to `'a`. Sound only because `inner_out` is None in
  pull mode, so the buffer borrows nothing local. Non-local: depends on `read_data`'s lifetime signature.
- permute_dims.rs:126, insert_dim.rs:176, remove_dim.rs:161 - calls of the above; established by constructors.
  Pull: InsertDim gives inserted (extent-1) dims stride 0. Push: RemoveDim gives removed dims stride 0.
- slice.rs:159 - `with_strides(stride * step)` on the inner bounding-box view. Relies on the PLAIN_READ meaning
  (non-local: set in storage/plain.rs and storage/scalar.rs, propagated by InsertDim/RemoveDim). Empty regions
  are excluded (slice.rs:147).
- slice.rs:197-198, roll.rs:124-125, tile.rs:182-184, reshape.rs:370-372, concatenate.rs:267-275,
  stack.rs:219-229 - `from_slice_mut(&mut out_buf[off..], strides)`: safe slicing (panics if off > len), then the
  inner writes through the strides. Assumes `out` covers the whole region (NOT established, see Contracts).
  Concatenate/Stack fast paths pass an exactly-sized packed slice (`off..off+size`) instead.
- broadcast.rs:151 - `with_strides` with 0 strides on broadcast dims; may relabel a writable PoolBuf with
  aliasing strides, contrary to `with_strides`' documented contract (buf.rs:202-207). Harmless unless something
  writes through a pull result (public `data_ptr_mut`, buf.rs:161, or reuse as `out`).
- broadcast.rs:156-163 - `out.copy_from(inner view, 0-stride src)`; src covers region by the pull contract.
- flip.rs:142-151, repeat.rs:186/195/197-205, tile.rs:219-229/262-272/285-295 - `NdCopier::copy` with
  `get_unchecked(src_off..)` / `get_unchecked_mut(dst_off..)`: an offset past the slice end is immediate UB, not a
  panic. src offsets are bounded by `idx < out_shape` (local reasoning); dst extents rely on `out` covering the
  region (caller); copy extents come from u64 math cast `as usize` (32-bit hazard).
- core_trait.rs:134 - default `OperandTyped::new_input(pull buffer)`, inherited by all shape ops; relies on the
  pull buffer being valid for the full index region.

## Edge-case surface
- Empty ranges: Roll(wrap)/Repeat/Tile/Reshape/Concatenate/Stack/Slice(stepped) return an unwritten
  `materialize_out_buf` early; Flip first pulls the (empty) inner region, then returns early (flip.rs:96-107);
  PermuteDims/RemoveDim/Slice(step 1)/Roll(non-wrap)/Tile(case A) forward the empty range; InsertDim
  short-circuits (insert_dim.rs:165-175); Broadcast still reads `0..1` on broadcast dims. Repeat/Tile with
  `repeats == 0` or input length 0 rely on that early return before `s / n` (repeat.rs:128) and `s % l`
  (tile.rs:146).
- 0-d arrays: NdIter over `[]` yields exactly one index (util/iter/nd.rs:582-584); Reshape `[] <-> [1,1]` and
  Flip of 0-d go through that. Roll/Repeat/Tile reject ndim 0 (dim < ndim). Stack of 0-d arrays gives `[n]`.
- Length-1 dims: InsertDim (pull) and RemoveDim (push) and Reshape (unmatched orig dims, reshape.rs:335-338) use
  stride 0 for extent-1 dims. Out buffers may legally have stride 0 on a length-1 dim; Stack/Concatenate fast paths
  test `is_contiguous` (exact default strides) so such outs take the general path.
- 0-stride input dims (Plain with zero-stride layout in tests, Scalar, Broadcast): Flip/Repeat/Tile read through
  them; Slice multiplies them (stays 0).
- NDIM_MAX=8: InsertDim/Stack check; Repeat/Tile need ndim <= 7. RemoveDim builds `dim_arr(dim.len())`
  (remove_dim.rs:58) before validating, and `SliceSpec::new`/`From<&[I]>` collect into a DimArray (slice.rs:246-262):
  both panic (not Err) for > 8 entries.
- Struct dtypes / inner shapes: all ops treat an element as `itemsize` opaque bytes; NdCopier picks a scalar
  copy by (itemsize, alignment) or an untyped copy (util/nd_copy.rs:30-40). Stack/Concatenate compare full `Dtype`.
- Overflow: `check_shape_overflow`/`try_product` short-circuit on a leading 0, so `[0, u64::MAX, 4]` passes while
  `[u64::MAX, 4, 0]` fails; code that multiplies a subset of dims (logical strides) can overflow. Concatenate sums
  lengths unchecked (concatenate.rs:111). `len as i64` in Roll (roll.rs:54) and slice resolution (slice.rs:365-367)
  is wrong for dims > i64::MAX (only reachable with u8/bool lazy broadcasts).
- 32-bit: requests whose element count exceeds `usize::MAX` are not rejected anywhere (array.rs:960 and
  to_ndarray_sub truncate too). Ops mix u64 index math with `as usize` extents/offsets (repeat.rs:164-194,
  tile.rs:205-284, concatenate.rs:248-261, stack.rs:193-215, flip.rs:82/139).
- Boundary-straddling reads: Concatenate pieces (borders, zero-length members in the middle), Roll wrap point
  (`s < shift < e`, roll.rs:93), Tile period (`s_in + total` vs `l`, cases A/B/C), Repeat group head/middle/tail
  (repeat.rs:209-233), Slice steps not dividing the length (`div_ceil`, slice.rs:403).

## Intentional behaviors
- Slice: step >= 1 only, negative steps rejected (slice.rs:26, 389-394; test `error_negative_step`). Bounds are
  strict - out-of-range start/end and start > end are errors, not clamped/empty (slice.rs:364-387; tests
  `resolve_rejects_*`); start == end and start == dim_len are accepted (`resolve_accepts_*`). Python allows only
  step 1 and checks strictly too (jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:118-121, 307-326).
- Broadcast requires equal ndim, no implicit leading dims (broadcast.rs:6-8, mod.rs:159); the Python layer
  prepends dims with InsertDim first (jix-py/src/ops/common/broadcast.rs:66-71).
- Tile never adds leading dims, unlike numpy (mod.rs:142-143, tile.rs:8-10). Repeat takes one scalar count.
  Both reject ndim == NDIM_MAX (tests `error_ndim_equals_ndim_max`).
- InsertDim uses numpy `expand_dims` output positions, duplicates rejected (insert_dim.rs:7-10). This replaced
  "gap index" semantics in adef94b; callers in jix-py were updated (jix-py/src/ops/reduction.rs:7-23).
- RemoveDim: only length-1 dims, duplicates rejected. Flip: duplicates rejected, empty dim list is a no-op.
  Roll: one dim, shift reduced modulo length, length 0 means shift 0 (roll.rs:50-55).
- Reshape has no `-1` in Rust (Python resolves it, jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:717-751) and is documented to
  read-amplify (reshape.rs:14-23, mod.rs:48-53).
- Rust Concatenate/Stack require identical dtypes (concatenate.rs:22-24, stack.rs:21); Python promotes first
  (bb1ee2c). Python requires equal ndim for both (documented deviation). Python `stack` of one array becomes
  InsertDim, `concatenate` of one array returns it unchanged (jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:872, 954).
- Flip, Repeat, Reshape, Concatenate, Stack, Roll(wrap), Tile(B/C) always materialize in pull mode; strides are
  usize so Flip cannot be a view. Broadcast push always copies (no forwarding of `out`).
- Block shape, fixed dims and scale weights are performance hints only (storage/params.rs:526-590); wrong values
  there are not correctness bugs (layout order is the exception, see Contracts).

### Changed in c009869 (#87) - supersedes conflicting statements above (line numbers above refer to bb1ee2c)
- Every shape op's read_data passes (index, itemsize) to `check_out_buf`, which now checks out's
  extent. Concatenate checks the concat-dim sum for overflow. Repeat no longer multiplies the stride
  of a length-1 out dim. Dims are capped at i64::MAX (affects roll's rem_euclid, slice resolve).

## Hot spots
- Push-mode offsets: for each split op, does every inner read land at `out + sum(offset_d * out_stride_d)` with the
  correct per-dim stride, and do the pieces tile the region exactly once? Check with permuted / padded `out`
  strides and with sub-reads from `to_ndarray_buf_slow_dyn` (array.rs:1048+), which pass sub-buffers of a larger
  `out`.
- Reshape (reshape.rs:290-375): the read-time match scan differs from the constructor's (reshape.rs:67-79: no
  length check, no advance on match). Is the `flat` decomposition (355-360, which omits matched dims) correct for
  every matched/unmatched mix? It is safe today only because a mismatch advances `orig_dim_idx` to the end
  (reshape.rs:305), so matched dims are always a prefix with exactly equal lengths. Any "fix" to the scan must
  revisit `flat`.
- Slice plain fast path (slice.rs:145-160): which storages can carry PLAIN_READ through InsertDim/RemoveDim, and
  does each one's pull read really return a borrowed view covering the bounding box? What about Scalar (one item,
  0 strides)?
- Repeat `copy_region` (repeat.rs:155-207): (ndim+1)-d split with stride `out_strides[k] * n` and 0 source stride;
  check `first_out_k - s`, `p_end_tail`, and the `g_count == 1` vs head/middle/tail branches for every
  `s mod n`, `e mod n`.
- Tile cases (tile.rs:150-297): exact case boundaries (`s_in + total <= l`, `total <= l`), Case C head/middle/
  tail extents vs `out_shape`, and the (ndim+1)-d middle copy (`src_dim` mapping, stride 0 at position k).
- Concatenate (concatenate.rs:212-279): `first_arr` linear vs binary search, zero-length members, the
  `inner_contiguous` condition (output dims before concat dim <= 1) vs Stack's `in_place` (array dims, stack.rs:198).
- Flip (flip.rs:87-151): mirrored inner range `[L-e, L-s)` and `dst_off = (len-1-idx)*stride`.
- Spec propagation: does every op produce a valid layout-order permutation and per-dim arrays of length ndim
  (InsertDim splice 104-113, RemoveDim `out_dim` 100-112, Stack shift+insert 127-131, Reshape `one_to_one`
  112-136, Concatenate `max_cost_layout_order`)?
- Recent churn: InsertDim semantics change (adef94b) - any remaining caller still passing gap indices? Stack/
  concatenate promotion (bb1ee2c) is Python-side only; core still trusts the runtime dtype check.

### Suspicions (unverified)
- reshape.rs:290-308 (also 67-79) - perf, not correctness: an unmatched new dim advances the scan to the end, so
  `[12]->[3,4]` or `[2,6]->[12]` match nothing and Reshape issues one inner read per element (the comment at
  reshape.rs:194-198 claims trailing dims match).
- slice.rs:320 - `Bound::Included(&e) => Some(e as i64 + 1)`: `..=-1` resolves to end 0 (empty) instead of the
  last element and `-3..=-1` errors; `as i64` also turns u64/usize bounds > i64::MAX negative, and `+ 1`
  overflows at i64::MAX.
- slice.rs:156-158 - `inner.strides()[dim] * step` is unchecked; a huge step with output length 1 (e.g.
  `i64::MAX`) over a Plain inner overflows (debug panic) on valid input.
- concatenate.rs:111 - `shape[dim] += shape_i[dim]` before `check_shape_overflow`; with u8/bool lazy inputs the sum
  can exceed u64: debug panic, release wrap (wrong shape, non-monotonic `borders`).
- tile.rs:205-229, repeat.rs:164-205 - 32-bit: `out_shape` is truncated by `as usize` (here and in
  `to_ndarray_sub`) but Case C / middle copy extents come from untruncated u64 math; e.g. u8 broadcast to
  `[2^31+4]`, `.tile(2, 0).to_ndarray()` allocates 8 bytes and NdCopier writes 2^31+4 (heap overflow).
- buf.rs:282-297 - `check_out_buf` never checks extent, and safe code can obtain a writable `StridedBuf` (a pull
  result backed by a PoolBuf). Passing a small pull result as `out` of a larger safe `to_ndarray_buf` lets
  Flip/Repeat/Tile write past it with `get_unchecked_mut` + NdCopier (safe-API UB).
- repeat.rs:181 - `out_strides[k] * n as usize` is computed even when `g_len == 1`; a large `repeats` with a large
  caller stride on dim k overflows (debug panic, value unused), and `n as usize` truncates on 32-bit.
- remove_dim.rs:58 - `dim_arr(dim.len(), ..)` asserts `<= NDIM_MAX` before validation, so `RemoveDim::new`
  (Result-returning) panics on > 8 dims, e.g. repeated ones.
- roll.rs:54 - `shift.rem_euclid(len as i64)` gives a wrong modulus for len > i64::MAX and panics for
  `len == u64::MAX` with `shift == i64::MIN`.
- reshape.rs:66 - `default_logical_strides(new_shape)` is unchecked; a zero-element reshape to `[0, u64::MAX, 4]`
  passes the `try_product` equality (short-circuit at the leading 0) and then overflows (debug panic).
- jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:314 - `start_norm >= len` rejects start == len, so `a[0:0]`, `a[n:]` and even
  `a[:]` on a zero-length dim raise IndexError, while core Slice accepts start == dim_len.

## Review units
Line counts exclude the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the bottom of each file (use those tests freely).

shape-ops-forwarders (~1010 lines): mod.rs:1-192, permute_dims.rs:1-171, insert_dim.rs:1-230,
remove_dim.rs:1-215, broadcast.rs:1-201, storage/buf.rs:321-368. Consult storage/buf.rs, storage/core_trait.rs,
storage/params.rs, storage/plain.rs, storage/scalar.rs.
- Is the buf.rs:364 lifetime transmute sound for every caller, and are the two stride closures exact inverses?
- InsertDim/RemoveDim: are `original_dims` / `dims_mapping` and both stride maps right for unsorted, adjacent and
  leading/trailing dims, in pull and push mode?
- InsertDim/RemoveDim keep PLAIN_READ: does every consumer of that flag (slice.rs:146, array.rs:964) stay correct?
- Broadcast pull hands out 0 strides (possibly on a writable PoolBuf); push copies. Any path that writes through
  or forwards such a buffer?
- Spec derivation: layout-order permutation validity and per-dim arrays of length ndim in all four ops.

shape-ops-slice-reshape (~820 lines): slice.rs:1-406, reshape.rs:1-411. Consult storage/buf.rs,
storage/params.rs, util/mod.rs, util/iter/nd.rs, jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:166-353.
- `DimSlice::resolve` and the `From<range>` conversions: negative, inclusive, huge (> i64::MAX) bounds.
- Stepped slice: steps that do not divide the length, sub-ranges of the view, the general path's per-item
  sub-buffers in push mode with permuted/padded `out`.
- Plain fast path: bounding box math (slice.rs:149-158), stride*step overflow, inner kinds that carry PLAIN_READ.
- Reshape read: correctness of matched/unmatched split and `flat` decomposition for size-1 dims, 0-d shapes,
  and orig dims skipped by the scan; `orig_strides` for push.
- Reshape::new: unchecked logical strides / `try_product` with zero-size dims; constructor vs read-time scan.

shape-ops-copy-ops (~970 lines): flip.rs:1-185, roll.rs:1-175, repeat.rs:1-273, tile.rs:1-335. Consult
storage/buf.rs, util/nd_copy.rs, util/mod.rs, array.rs:740-1060.
- Every `get_unchecked(_mut)` offset: is it provably within the slice for all ranges, incl. 0-stride inner dims?
- Flip: mirrored inner range and `dst_off` for partial sub-ranges on several flipped dims at once.
- Roll: wrap split at `shift` (roll.rs:93-141) - lengths, dst offsets, non-wrap `j_start` when `e <= shift`.
- Repeat: head/middle/tail cover each output position exactly once; (ndim+1)-d copy shapes and strides.
- Tile: case A/B/C boundaries, Case C extents vs `out_shape`, the synthesized stride-0 dim.
- 32-bit: u64 extents cast with `as usize` vs the truncated destination size.

shape-ops-join (~570 lines + sequence glue): concatenate.rs:1-308, stack.rs:1-261,
util/arr_sequence.rs:1-93, util/arr_sequence.rs:600-664. Consult storage/buf.rs, storage/params.rs,
ops/into_type.rs, jix-py/src/ops/shape_ops.rs:842-965.
- `borders` construction (unchecked sum) and lookup (linear vs `partition_point`), zero-length members.
- `inner_contiguous` / `in_place` fast paths: is the packed slot exactly the sub-array's bytes in `out`?
- Per-member sub-index and buffer offset with permuted / padded `out` strides; stack dim at 0, middle, ndim.
- ElementType soundness: can a sequence reach `Stack`/`Concatenate` with mismatched runtime dtypes but a typed ET?
- Spec combine (`combine_block_layout`, `combine_select_hints`, Stack layout shift) yields valid arrays.
